title: Same-year flow pairs had 1.7% higher mean seven-day peaks than shuffled pairs at three Arctic gauges in 1980-2011
abstract: We tested whether same-year pairing increased peaks of summed discharge at Ob-Salekhard, Lena-Kyusyur and Yenisey-Igarka. In 31 common certified years from 1980 to 2011, the mean April-August seven-day peak was 249,541 cubic metres per second. Independent year pairing within three periods gave 245,284, a 1.74% difference, with conditional two-sided p = 0.0368. Equal seasonal volumes retained a 1.63% excess. Exact calculation confirmed the null mean. Leave-one-year checks retained positive differences. Five-year pairing and circular shifts supported the direction. This is a small association under conditional exchangeability, not a causal effect or a measured coastal pulse. Data overlap earlier timing studies; the new test concerns cross-river dependence. Short records, regulation, serial dependence, source error and absent travel times limit inference. Code, provenance, aggregate results, null draws and a figure are included. Raw data and annual tables remain external.

display.caption: Observed mean yearly seven-day peaks and independent within-period year-pairing distributions, before and after seasonal-volume normalization. Histograms are conditional null reference distributions, not confidence intervals.
